hostname.description: Hostname visible inside the container and used for reverse DNS lookup

boot.description: Boot the container's init system as PID 1; requires a complete OS tree (not just a single binary)

ephemeral.description: Discard all filesystem changes on shutdown; useful for stateless or immutable containers

private_users.description: User namespace mode: 'no' (none), 'yes' (fixed mapping), 'pick' (auto-select safe range), or a numeric UID base like '100000'

user.description: Run the container main process as this user; leave empty to run as root

working_directory.description: Initial working directory for the container process; leave empty for the system default

environment_vars.description: Environment variables to inject into all container processes

capabilities.description: Additional Linux capabilities to grant beyond the default bounding set (e.g. CAP_NET_ADMIN)

drop_capabilities.description: Linux capabilities to remove from the default bounding set (e.g. CAP_NET_RAW CAP_SYS_ADMIN)

no_new_privileges.description: Block privilege escalation via setuid binaries or file capabilities inside the container

limit_nofile.description: Maximum number of open file descriptors per process inside the container (ulimit -n)

limit_nproc.description: Maximum number of processes or threads the container may spawn (ulimit -u)

read_only.description: Mount the container root filesystem read-only; combine with Volatile or BindReadOnly for mutable state paths

volatile.description: Volatile mode: 'no' = fully persistent, 'yes' = tmpfs replaces the entire root, 'state' = tmpfs overlays /var only

bind_mounts.description: Host paths to bind-mount into the container with read-write access

bind_read_only_mounts.description: Host paths to bind-mount into the container with read-only access

tmpfs_mounts.description: Paths inside the container to mount as fresh ephemeral tmpfs on each start (e.g. /tmp, /run)

network_private.description: Run the container in its own isolated network namespace (strongly recommended)

virtual_ethernet.description: Create a veth pair between host and container for network connectivity; effective only when Private=yes

bridge.description: Host bridge interface to attach the container veth to (e.g. br0); leave empty for a point-to-point veth pair

network_zone.description: systemd-networkd zone name; the daemon auto-creates a bridge and manages DHCP/routing (leave empty to configure networking manually)

port_forwards.description: Host-to-container port forwarding rules; only effective when Private=yes

host_port.description: Port number on the host to forward from

container_port.description: Port number inside the container to forward to

macvlan_interfaces.description: Host network interfaces to clone as MACVLAN links inside the container (e.g. eth0)
